profile.reading: DartPoints operates an edge colocation data center at 100 Technology Drive, Suite C, in the Biltmore Park Technology Center in Asheville, North Carolina. DartPoints is a Dallas, Texas-headquartered colocation and interconnection company focused on secondary and tertiary US markets. This Asheville facility traces its origin to Immedion, a Greenville, South Carolina-headquartered colocation and managed-services provider founded in 2007 that operated eight data centers across seven markets before DartPoints announced its acquisition of the company on March 16, 2021, a deal DartPoints described as more than doubling its edge interconnection footprint. Notably, DartPoints' more recent capital raise, a strategic growth investment from NOVA Infrastructure reported at more than 250 million dollars combined with Orion Infrastructure Capital and announced around April 2025, specifically included DartPoints acquiring the underlying real estate for this Asheville building, suggesting the company had previously leased rather than owned the property. The facility spans 23,000 square feet of white space with an 11,200-square-foot data hall, drawing 1.5 megawatts of utility power against a 296-kilowatt critical IT load, backed by 2,050 kilowatts of generator capacity and 975 kilowatts of UPS capacity, cooled by 330 tons of N+1 redundant capacity, with 7 on-site network providers. Asheville's city council passed a year-long moratorium on new data center development in June 2025 over community concerns about energy consumption, though available coverage does not name DartPoints specifically in connection with that policy, and the moratorium applies to new construction rather than this existing facility. As is standard industry practice, tenant identities are not publicly disclosed, and no Uptime Institute Tier certification level is stated for this building.

reading.body:
DartPoints Asheville publishes 1.5 MW of IT capacity, making it the fifth-largest disclosed facility in North Carolina and accounting for 3 percent of the state's 50.3 MW of published data center power.

The facility occupies 11,200 square feet at Biltmore Park Technology Center with N+1 backup power covering 2,050 kW of generator and 975 kW of UPS capacity. At typical AI training density, 1.5 MW supports approximately 37 racks or 300 accelerators. Seven network providers across five fiber entries provide connectivity options.

North Carolina has 19 mapped facilities, but only five publish capacity figures. DartPoints Asheville is substantially smaller than the state's leading facilities and represents a sparse set of locations with disclosed specifications. The operator's own site does not indicate which workloads currently run here or name specific tenants.

This facility's backup power budget suggests readiness for continuous operation, a requirement for any infrastructure hosting production AI workloads. Whether that capacity is currently in use remains unpublished.
